gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the wireless Hall effect boards side by side with today's price and each maker's own per-mode polling statement: Aula Hero75 HE states up to 8,000 Hz on both USB-C and 2.4 GHz and 125 Hz on Bluetooth at $83.03, Keychron K2 HE states 1,000 Hz at $103.99, and Gamakay's three tri-mode boards run $63.99 to $89.99 (all read 2026-11-21).
standout_why: Compared against the Aula Hero75 HE store page (in ChatGPT's results, uncited), whose text I read, and against the Attack Shark X65/X68 Pro HE pages as ChatGPT quoted them; I could not open the Attack Shark pages myself (connection failed on every attempt). The Aula page already states its own 8,000 Hz wired/2.4 GHz and 125 Hz Bluetooth split, and ChatGPT's answer already carries Attack Shark's 8,000 Hz wired to 1,000 Hz wireless drop. What those pages lack is any other maker's figure or a price comparison. The Verge page (blocked to me) is a Keychron deal post; the manuals.plus Attack Shark PDF is image-only with no readable text. So rivals hold the per-model parts; only the priced cross-brand table is new. I could not source a per-mode polling statement for the Gamakay TK75HE V2 or NS75, which caps how far this angle can decide the pick.
decides: It confirms the answer is 'yes on 2.4 GHz, model-dependent on polling' and narrows the buy. Among boards whose maker statement I read today, only the Aula Hero75 HE ($83.03) states 8,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz; the Keychron K2 HE ($103.99) states 1,000 Hz and costs more; the Aula Hero 68 HE ($69.46) is wired-only and the Gamakay TK68 HE ($79.99) is sold out. For a linkable pick, the Gamakay TK75 TMR ($89.99) only wins if the 8,000 Hz-on-2.4 GHz figure in our record (attributed there to HLPlanet, not re-opened by me) is verified by another angle; the NS75 ($63.99) and NS68 tri-mode are the low-price tri-mode options, but I read no per-mode statement for them. Attack Shark stays unpriced, so it cannot be a table row from this angle.
